adminComparison.note: JS payloads are near-identical (frontend 2,516,529 B vs admin 2,513,808 B) and module counts are close (13,905 vs 13,986). The frontend's larger total (4,975,690 B vs 2,603,266 B) is not code: a single 2,037,251 B .mp4 static asset accounts for 40.9% of its output bytes. Entry chunks are comparable (57,764 B vs 62,413 B pre-optimization admin; queue #7 later cut the admin entry to 41,347 B - no equivalent pass has been run on the frontend).

assessment.text: Total output size is dominated by one static asset: a single .mp4 of 2,037,251 B (40.9% of all bytes). It is not JavaScript and not part of the bundle graph; any reduction is an asset-pipeline question (compression, poster/preload strategy), not a code-splitting one. Recorded for completeness; no action taken.

A standalone validator chunk of 126,673 B ships in the frontend build - the same library queue #7 reduced in admin by switching to deep imports (validator/es/lib/*). Whether the frontend's validator usage is equally narrow (a handful of functions) was not audited in this report-only slice; it is the most direct candidate for a future frontend optimization pass mirroring GA-P2-PERF-BUNDLE-01. Not changed here.

UserContext (269,898 B) is the largest shared chunk, mirroring the admin structure. The frontend's localized-strings modules statically embed all locales behind a synchronous API (39 modules brought to ar==fr parity in queue #5), so per-language splitting carries the same behavior-preservation caveat recorded for admin in GA-P2-PERF-BUNDLE-01 (notDone): it requires restructuring module shape plus async language loading. Not attempted.

The largest JS chunk, Bookings (429,445 B), and Map (163,472 B) are separate route-level chunks, not part of the 57,764 B entry; the entry path itself is lean and comparable to admin's. No duplicate-import smoking gun was found at chunk level (vendor appears once, 178,287 B - the identical size to admin's vendor chunk, i.e. the shared dependency set is bundled once per app as expected).

crossChecks.note: The fresh host build's entry chunk is byte-named identically to the entry the running bc-frontend container serves on :8080 (the queue #6 layered build of this same source), which verifies the baseline measures the real, non-empty production build output - the queue #4 empty-shell failure mode (host build without .env) does not apply: frontend/.env was present and the outputs agree.

method: Official `npm run build` in frontend/ (ts:build + vite build), byte totals over frontend/build/ (files, total bytes, JS/CSS split, entry file size from build/index.html, top chunks by size). Identical script and measures as the GA-P2-PERF-01 / GA-P2-PERF-BUNDLE-01 admin baselines, so the two apps are directly comparable. frontend/.env was already present on the host (created during queue #5), so the host build ran with the same env the Docker build uses; no .env file was created or modified by this slice.
scopeNote: Report-only baseline. No code was changed and no optimization was performed in this slice. This is the customer-frontend counterpart of the GA-P2-PERF-01 admin baseline (artifacts/perf-index-review-01.json, key adminBundleBaseline), which GA-P2-PERF-BUNDLE-01 (queue #7) could not extend because the frontend had never been baselined (scorecard GA-P10-READINESS-SCORECARD-01, list (c)).
